author: blu
body: Do NOT restore a binary search here. This was one until 2026-07-28 (main 11369) and it silently found only some of its names: a binary search requires the list to be ordered by the comparison it searches with, and the list is written alphabetically while text-compare orders by CCE, which numbers letters by frequency. `i` is 19 and `b` is 32, so `int-mod` sorts before `bit-and` under the comparator and after it in the list. Names past the first inversion were unreachable, and an unreachable builtin does not fail loudly -- it falls through to the ordinary apply path and emits a call to a function the target language has never heard of. Measured per plug by codex/plugs/test-input/builtin-reach.codex, a probe that cites nothing so its calls reach this table. Thirteen plugs carried the defect. A linear scan has no ordering invariant to get wrong and this runs once per call site at transpile time.

author: fester
body: The correction needs "if the remainder came back negative, add the divisor's magnitude", and this emitter cannot express that test. `bab-bin-op-card` maps IrEq, IrNotEq, IrLt, IrGt, IrLtEq and IrGtEq ALL to the single `-` card, so a comparison here is a subtraction and nothing distinguishes "is negative" from "is zero". Writing the branch anyway would mean inventing a polarity for `CF` that no card in this file establishes, in a deck no machine executes.

author: fester
body: So the divergence is confined and written down: int-mod on this target answers the sign of the dividend, and is correct only where the dividend is non-negative. Giving the Analytical Engine real relational operators is the prerequisite, and it would fix every `if` in every emitted deck, not only this one.
